clue.text: Choose filling food for VIPs seated here?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the place, so it stands for the noun

indicators.note: one word filling another sits inside it, the other wrapping round

parts.note: table in the sense of the food served, as in 'keeps a good table'
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: A dinner plan: picking the fare for the dignitaries' table at a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food' for TABLE uses the old sense of the meals a household provides; 'filling' looks like hearty food but places one word inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: At a formal dinner or wedding the top table is the raised one where the guests of honour sit.

clue.text: Source of upset entering streetcar, a deeply distressing experience

indicators.note: something entering goes inside the word that follows

parts.note: a streetcar is a tram

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so take its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of upset
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone upset on a tram ride that proves a horrible ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside TRAM, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is the psychological term for a shocking event that leaves lasting emotional damage.

clue.text: Average sum for chief

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
a sum is an amount

explanation.surface: Arithmetic in a boss's report: the mean figure is what matters most.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means of supreme importance, the same adjective sense as chief or principal.

clue.text: Dr No, I suspect, shown in advertisement for a robot

indicators.note: being shown in something places it inside that word

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement

indicators.note: a suspect version is not to be trusted as given, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: letters of Dr, No and I to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A Bond villain apparently fronting a commercial for a mechanical man.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr No is the villain of the first James Bond film; here his name is just letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a robot built to look and act like a human being.

clue.text: Weird tale about sailor going in that place for fish

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters surround what follows
going in places the sailor inside the next word

parts.note: letters of tale rearranged

indicators.note: weird means strange or odd, so these letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: there means in that place
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A strange yarn about a seaman heading to some spot to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the sailor goes into 'that place' first, and the whole lot sits within the shuffled tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Leatherjacket is the name of several tough-skinned fish, such as the filefish.

clue.text: Swift runner loses heart getting duck

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter is removed

parts.note: a scooter is a fast-moving small vehicle

explanation.surface: A sprinter who loses nerve and comes away with nothing, a duck in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOOTER drops its middle O. 'Duck' looks like a cricket score or a dodge, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark-plumaged sea duck of northern coasts.

clue.text: Strong fabric, fine in wind

parts.note: chino is a hard-wearing twilled cotton cloth
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A sturdy cloth that holds up well in a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinook is a warm dry wind that blows down the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Turn in wind

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a turn or bend, as in a road
second meaning: to wind or coil, the verb pronounced to rhyme with mind

explanation.surface: A change of direction caused by a gust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as the breeze, but it is the verb meaning to coil.
explanation.definitionFit: Twist works as a noun for a turn or bend and as a verb meaning to wind or wrap round.

clue.text: Rush over dropping in new gear for the clothing business

indicators.note: turned over, the word is read from its end back to its start
dropping in means placing this inside the following letters
a new version of the word has its letters rearranged

parts.note: letters of gear rearranged
to dart is to rush

explanation.surface: Hurrying to deliver new outfits to the fashion industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' looks like the clothes themselves, but it is only letters to shuffle. Rag trade is informal British for the garment industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag trade is a slang name for the industry that designs, makes and sells clothes.

clue.text: Biting cold in desert

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a desert is arid, dry
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: The sharp chill of a desert night.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid describes a sharp, pungent, stinging smell or taste, the sense of biting as harsh.

clue.text: Sailor's reportedly sick of this outdoor pursuit

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; AB'S is spoken as the first syllable

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so go by the sound of the words

parts.note: ailing means sick

explanation.surface: A seaman is said to be fed up with this activity.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, AB'S AILING sounds like ABSEILING.
explanation.definitionFit: Abseiling, descending a rock face on a rope, is a popular open-air adventure activity.

clue.text: A bistro may make one check order

definitions.note: a clause describing the thing, standing for the noun

parts.note: a service is a check on a car or machine
a charge is an order or command

explanation.surface: A restaurant may make a single cheque out to order, for a meal ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' and 'order' look like a restaurant bill and a food order; they are a maintenance inspection and a command.
explanation.definitionFit: Many restaurants add a service charge, a percentage of the bill paid in lieu of tipping.

clue.text: Huge insect discovered by male, American

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
AM is the abbreviation for American
a moth is an insect

explanation.surface: A man from the US finds an enormous bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered by' places the insect after the other pieces, as if found by them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth, from the extinct giant elephant, is used as an adjective meaning enormous.

clue.text: Farmyard cock and duck in list

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Animals on a farm inventory: a cockerel and a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' sounds like the farmyard bird; it is the cricket score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooster is the chiefly American word for a male domestic chicken.

clue.text: Rum do led, I know, to change in play

indicators.note: changing the letters means putting them into a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd party is said to have prompted a change in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' is British slang for strange and 'do' for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Under Milk Wood is Dylan Thomas's radio play about a Welsh fishing village.

clue.text: Vulnerable in hot, sticky, French city

indicators.note: a sticky situation is awkward and messy, signalling the letters are muddled

parts.note: letters of in and hot rearranged
Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Exposed on a sweltering, humid day in a Riviera resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticky' reads as humid weather, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on thin ice is an idiom for being in a risky, precarious position.

clue.text: Ten in game bid strangely — an assortment of diverse people

indicators.note: strangely means in an unusual way, so the letters are put in an unusual order
one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: letters of game and bid rearranged
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: An odd bid at a card table, with a varied crowd of players.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed bag is an idiom for a varied collection of people or things.

clue.text: Similarly situated, as the three with Montmorency were?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sharing the same predicament

definitions.text: as the three with Montmorency were?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally, the three men of Jerome K. Jerome's novel shared one rowing boat with their dog

explanation.walkthrough: Montmorency is the fox terrier in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat, about a Thames boating trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means facing the same difficulties as others, and the novel's trio were literally sharing one craft.

clue.text: Former partner given sufficient warning

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
ample means sufficient or more than enough

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse gets plenty of notice of what is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: An example, as in making an example of someone, serves as a caution to others.

clue.text: Look at newspaper endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone reads the paper on and on without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something is to watch or notice it carefully.

clue.text: Failing to change sides

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fault or flaw, as a noun
second meaning: to desert one's country or party for another

explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' reads as a verb tied to the rest; it is a noun meaning a weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: Defect is a noun for an imperfection and a verb, stressed differently, for going over to the opposition.

clue.text: Designate member to go aboard English vessel

indicators.note: going aboard a vessel puts one inside it

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
an arm is a limb, a member of the body
an ark is a boat, like Noah's

explanation.surface: Appointing a club member to board a British ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a club member; here it is a limb of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark is to set aside or assign something for a particular purpose.

clue.text: A Parisian in bar getting a number of drinks

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a rod is a bar of metal or wood
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in a pub buys drinks for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' sounds like the pub; it is a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A round is a set of drinks bought for everyone in a group at once.

clue.text: Unfriendly landlord, extremely unpleasant losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a host is a landlord, as of an inn
vile means extremely unpleasant

explanation.surface: A pub landlord so nasty he gets his head bitten off.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile describes antagonistic, unfriendly behaviour, like an enemy.

clue.text: Flag down taxi initially engaged by nobleman

parts.note: feeling down is feeling blue

indicators.note: something engaged by another is held inside it

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter only

parts.note: first letter of taxi

explanation.surface: A lord hailing a cab, waving it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag down' reads as one phrase, hailing a taxi; split it, flag is the definition and down gives BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Peter is a blue and white signal flag hoisted when a ship is about to sail.

clue.text: Inflate article during climb

indicators.note: something happening during another sits within it

parts.note: to rise is to climb
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Puffing up a piece of kit on the way up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise prices or figures is to increase them, the economic sense of inflate.

clue.text: Ingenious device engineer tagged

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so the letters are built into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever contraption that an engineer has labelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like the person who tagged it; it is a verb telling you to rebuild the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small clever mechanical tool or appliance.

clue.text: Chaps, in principle, responsible for flat

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Men who are, in principle, in charge of an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a flat or set of rooms in a large shared building, especially in Scotland.
